= USD Render =
#type: node
#context: out
#internal: usdrender
#icon: ROP/usdrender
#since: 18.0

"""Renders an output image from the stage generated by a LOP network."""


== Overview ==

This node writes the USD generated by a LOP network to a temp file, then launches an external process (by default, [husk|/ref/utils/husk]) to render an image or image sequence from the USD.

Rendering uses the same USD interface (Hydra) as is used to render the Solaris viewport, but instead of displaying the generated pixel buffers, the renderer saves them to image files. You can choose to render using any Hydra client registered with USD.


== Configuration ==

Traditionally in Houdini, the renderer was configured using parameters on the render node. In USD, however, render settings are stored in a `RenderSettings` primitive in the scene tree.

See the help for the [Render Settings LOP|Node:lop/rendersettings], [Render Product LOP|Node:lop/renderproduct], and [Render Var LOP|Node:lop/rendervar] for more information about creating USD render settings.

The parameters on this node primarily deal with launching the render process, with just a few options to override key options for controlling the render.


== Available renderers == (list)

* The list of renderers is filtered based on the data returned by the `usdrenderers.py` script. The [husk|/ref/utils/husk] utility, and by extension the USD Render node, only support renderers that can generate AOV buffers (that is, renderers whose `aovsupport` attribute is `True`).

:include /solaris/view#render_delegate_tip:

@parameters

Render to Disk:
    #id: execute

    Renders with the last render control settings. This blocks Houdini until the render completes.

Render to MPlay:
    #id: renderpreview

    Render directly into an MPlay preview window, instead of to an image file. (You can save the image to disk from inside MPlay.)

Render to Disk in Background:
    #id: executebackground

    Renders with the last render control settings in a background process.

:include usd#renderdialog:

Valid Frame Range:
    #id: validframerange
    Render Current Frame:
        Render the current frame number (in the playbar).

    Render Frame Range:
        Render each frame in the range set by the __Start/End/Inc__ parameters below.

    Render Frame Range (Strict):
        The "Render Frame Range" option may generate frames outside the given range if they're requested by a render dependency. If you choose this option, this node will never render frames outside the given range.

	Render Frame Range From Stage:
		Examines the USD stage of the source LOP node for a start and end timecode value. These are used as the start and end of the frame range to render. If the stage does not have this metadata set, executing a render operation will result in an error.

:include usd#f:

:include usd#foffset:

Render All Frames with a Single Process:
    #id: allframesatonce

    Render all frames with a single process. Default is off, which causes a new render process to be invoked to render each frame. To render multiple frames with a single process, the render process renders an image, then advances the time on the scene and renders the next image (just like how the Solaris viewport plays back animation). If there is a lot of data shared between frames, this can render significantly faster compared to rendering a single frame per process.

    If the invocation of a render process is disabled, this setting still affects the behavior of the USD save process. If each frame's USD is being authored to a separate file or directory, this setting has no effect. But if every frame is configured to author the USD files to the same location, leaving this option off will overwrite the USD data with each frame, leaving only the final frame's data in the USD files on disk. Enable this option to have each frame's data merged with all the previous frames' data, resulting in a USD file that contains data for all the frames.

Render Delegate:
    #id: renderer
    The Hydra client to use to render the images. Alternate Hydra clients must be registered with Houdini's USD libraries. See how the node gets the [list of available renderers|#list] above.

    When `husk` renders an image, it will choose the render delegate based on the following rules:
    * The delegate specified with the `--renderer` command line option will be used
    * If there's no command line, `husk` will look for the `husk:default_delegate` property on the `RenderSettings` primitive
    - If there's no property on the `RenderSettings` primitive, the value of the `HOUDINI_HUSK_DEFAULT_DELEGATE` environment variable will be used

    When you set this parameter to something other than __Default Delegate__, the ROP will add the `--renderer` command line option, forcing `husk` to use the render delegate selected.  With __Default Delegate__, `husk` will choose the delegate from the `RenderSettings" prim or the environment variable.

Enable GPU Delegates:
    #id: husk_gpu
    `husk` normally doesn't support delegates which require a GPU rendering context for rendering.  This allows `husk` to run on headless machines.  Enabling this option will cause `husk` to try to create a GPU rendering context so that delegates like `HdStormRendererPlugin` can be used as delegates.

    A GPU rendering context allows a device or software to send commands to the GPU and control the state of a GPU. A context requires a GPU and the appropriate drivers and libraries installed. However, machines on render farms often don't have a GPU rendering context.

    NOTE:
        This option is not required for Karma XPU rendering!

LOP Path:
    #id: loppath

    Render the USD stage output by this node. If this is blank, the node uses the node with the display flag.

Render Settings:
    #id: rendersettings

    Scene graph pattern specifying the `RenderSettings` prims to render with. Husk supports running multiple renders with different render settings prims from one process. When evaluating this pattern with __Render existing file__ enabled, the specified file is opened as a USD stage with a population mask limiting the stage to the `/Render` branch, and the pattern is evaluated on that stage. If this is blank, the node looks for default render settings on the root prim. If the root prim has no render settings, the node will use default settings.

Render Pass:
    #id: renderpass

    Scene graph pattern to the `RenderPass` prims to use for specifying object visibility etc. Husk supports running multiple renders with different render passes (each specifying their own render settings prim) from one process. If this is blank, the default setting, the render will continue with no pass (i.e., all contents will be rendered).

Override Camera:
    #id: override_camera

    Scene graph path to the `Camera` prim to render from. If this is blank, the node uses the camera specified on the render settings primitive.

Override Output Image:
    #id: outputimage

    If this is not blank, render to this file path instead of the output specified in the `RenderSettings` prim. When starting a new render process for each frame, this parameter can use standard Houdini variables such as `$F4` to specify unique per-frame image files. When `Render All Frames with a Single Process` is enabled, this parameter must pass an un-expanded frame specifier (such as `$F4` or `<FF>`) to `husk`. This may require the use of a backslash to prevent variable expansion when evaluating the parameter.

Override Resolution:
    #id: override_res

    Override the resolution by either scaling the USD resolution by a percentage or by specifying a specific resolution.

Resolution Scale:
    #id: res_scale

    Specify a scale (as a percentage) for the output resolution.

Resolution:
    #id: res_user

    Specify a resolution explicitly.

== Husk ==
#id: husk

=== Rendering ===

Disable Motion Blur:
    #id: husk_instantshutter

    Disable motion blur by setting the camera to have an instantaneous shutter time.

Disable Hydra Generative Procedurals:
    #id: husk_disablehdgp

    Disable Hydra Generative Procedurals from being executed at render-time.
    
    Note that this only controls the resolving Scene Index created by husk. If an additional resolver is created via some other means, it will not be suppressed by this parameter.

Headlight Mode:
    #id: husk_headlight
    When `husk` determines there are no lights on a stage, it will add a headlight.  In some cases, `husk` may not properly identify geometry light sources and add a headlight erroneously.  This option overrides the default behavior, explicitly telling `husk` what type of headlight to create (if any).

Population Mask:
    #id: husk_populationmask

    *Comma* or *space* separated list of primitives that have to included in the render. If this is enabled, all other primitives will be omitted.

Include Render Settings and Cameras:
    #id: husk_rendersettingsandcams

    Enabling this will append all cameras found in the stage, as well as the render settings (assuming they're in `/Render`) to the population mask.

Mute Layers:
    #id: husk_mutelayers
    Each enabled entry is passed to the render command line as a `--mute-layer` option, muting the named USD layer when loading the stage. Layer muting prevents the named layer from contributing to the composed stage; this is equivalent to the [Mute Layers|Node:lop/configurestage] parameter on the Configure Stage LOP.

    Enable:
        Individual layer mute entries can be enabled or disabled with this toggle.

    Layer:
        The identifier of the USD layer to mute.

Purpose:
    #id: husk_purpose

    *Comma* separated list of purposes to render (from `geometry`, `guide`, `proxy`, and `render`). The default is `geometry,render`.

Complexity:
    #id: husk_complexity

    This setting is defined by USD and Hydra to control for the number of iterations to use to render "refine-able" (subdivision) surfaces. Karma mostly ignores this setting, since it measures the surface in screen space to decide how many iterations it needs to render the surface smoothly. Instead, *Karma uses this setting more like a subdivision on/off switch*. If this is set to __Low__ or __Medium__, Karma renders the (chunky) hull. If it is __High__ or __Very High__, Karma renders the (smooth) limit surface.

    Other renderers (such as RenderMan or Storm) will treat this setting differently, using it to determine subdivision quality. If you need to render the same scene in Karma and another renderer, remember to use __High__ or __Very High__ to make sure Karma renders subdivision surfaces smoothly.

Enable Legacy EXR Mode:
    #id: husk_legacyexr

    When saving OpenEXR images with multiple AOVs, `husk` will normally save the images using multi-part EXR files. This extension (introduced in 2013) lets programs read a single AOV without having to read the entire image.  This allows most software to work much more efficiently. Please note when you turn on __Enable Legacy EXR Mode__, `husk` will disable multi-part EXRs and save the files as a single-part image.

    Some applications have not transitioned to support multi-part images.  If your pipeline uses software that doesn't support OpenEXR v2.0, this option will force `husk` to write out images in an inefficient, but more compatible format.

Skip Existing Frames:
    #id: husk_skip_existing_frames

    Tell husk to skip rendering when the render product already exists on disk.

Delegate Products:
    Turn on render delegate products.  These allow render delegates to save non-raster products like deep images or photon maps.  These render products are render delegate specific.

Restart Delegate:
    Normally, when rendering sequences, `husk` uses UDS delta operations to make rendering more efficient.  The delegate is only told about scene data that changes frame-to-frame so it can share work between frames.

    This option will force the render delegate to be restarted when rendering sequences.

    Since restarting the delegate will cause the scene to be rebuilt, using this option can have significant performance impact and should only be used if required.

Snapshot Interval:
    When turned on, the renderer writes out a snapshot file and partial image at every interval of this many seconds.

Time Limit:
    When turned on, the renderer will terminate if the render time limit is exceeded. __Time Limit__ is measured in seconds. Note that `husk` will save the partial result before terminating.

Time Limit Per-Image:
    When rendering multiple frames in a single process (Render All Frames with a Single Process), the time limit specified is applied per image rather than the entire sequence of images.

=== Monitor ===

MPlay Monitor:
    #id: husk_mplay

    When rendering to disk, open an MPlay window to interactively monitor progress.

AOVs:
    This is the list of AOVs to display in the MPlay monitor.  Specifying `-` will monitor all AOVs.

Monitor Zoom:
    #id: husk_mplayzoom

    This is a zoom factor applied to the monitor.  The monitor will display images at a fraction of the full resolution while the image written to disk will be full resolution.

MPlay Session Name:
    #id: husk_mplayname

    When rendering to MPlay, all Houdini sessions will send the output to the same MPlay flipbook. This can be problematic when running multiple Houdini sessions. The MPlay Label lets you specify a label for the MPlay associated with the output driver. Only renders which match the given label will be sent to that MPlay.

    Houdini Process ID:
        Uses the operating system process identifier so that the MPlay flipbook will only accept renders from that Houdini session.

    HIP Name:
        Uses the `$HIPNAME` variable so the MPlay will only accept renders from the running `$HIP` file.

    Output Driver Name:
        The MPlay flipbook will only accept renders from the given output driver. For example, if you copy paste the output driver, each output driver will be sent to different MPlay flipbooks because the operators will have different names.

        If there are multiple Houdini sessions, there may be output drivers in the other session which match the same operator name.

        For example, say you have two output drivers: "High quality" and "Low Quality". If you set the MPlay Label to different values for the two output drivers, each render will be sent to different MPlay sessions.

=== Texture ===

This tab sets options to control OpenImageIO texturing.  Not all render delegates will respect these settings.

Maximum Resolution:
    #id: husk_tex_res

    Specify the maximum texture resolution for this render.

Texture Cache Memory:
    #id: husk_tex_memmode

    Specify the maximum memory used by the texture cache.
    * __Use Renderer's Default__.  Do not override the texture memory and let the renderer use its default.
    * __Explicit Memory in MB__.  Specify the number of MB of memory to reserve for the texture cache.
    * __Percentage of System Memory__.  Reserve a percentage of the system memory for the texture cache.

Cache Memory MB:
    #id: husk_tex_mem, husk_tex_mempct

    The memory to reserve for the OpenImageIO texture cache as either an explicit amount or a percentage of the system memory.

Max Open Files:
    #id: husk_tex_filemode

    Every operating system has a maximum number of files that can be open simultaneously, which also limits the number of _texture files_ that can be open at the same time.  This option lets you control how many files are reserved for the texture cache.
    * __Use Renderer's Default__.  Do not override the maximum file descriptor count and let the renderer use its default.
    * __Explicit Limit__.  Specify the maximum number of open files explicitly.
    * __Percentage of System Limit__.  Reserve a percentage of the system defined limit of file descriptors for the texture cache.
    * __Use All Available Except__.  Use all except the specified number of file descriptors.  This allows you to reserve some file descriptors for other uses, e.g. saving images or reading geometry.

Open Files:
    #id: husk_tex_files, husk_tex_filespct, husk_tex_filesreserve

    The file descriptors to reserve for the texture cache.

=== Python ===

Similar to how Houdini can run scripts during rendering, `husk` can also run Python scripts.  These Python scripts can access the USD stage using the `stage` variable in Python.

You can, for example, skip already rendered frames by specifying a __Husk Pre-Frame__ script. The script below skips frame #2. Change the script to your needs, save it and load it to __Husk Pre-Frame__.

{{{
    #!Python

    import sys
    import os
    import hou

    class SkipFrame(Exception):
        pass

    print("Run script:", sys.argv, hou.frame())

    if hou.frame() == 2:
        raise SkipFrame
}}}

Husk Post-Load:
    The Python script `husk` runs after the USD file has been loaded, but before any render settings have been configured.

Husk Pre-Render:
    The Python script `husk` runs before any rendering begins, but after render settings have been configured.

Husk Pre-Frame:
    The Python script `husk` runs before rendering each frame.

Husk Pre-Snapshot:
    The Python script `husk` runs before saving a snapshot image.

Husk Post-Snapshot:
    The Python script `husk` runs after saving a snapshot image.

Husk Post-Frame:
    The Python script `husk` runs after rendering each frame.  This is run after all render products are saved.

Husk Post-Render:
    The Python script `husk` runs after all rendering.


=== Tiles ===

Tiled Render:
    `husk` can break up a single large image into multiple tiles and render each tile independently.  It does this by overriding the `dataWindowNDC` setting defined on the render settings.

Render All Tiles and Stitch Final Image:
    Render a single by rendering multiple tiles in a single process.  Once all tiles are rendered, `husk` stitches them to make the final image.  This process is not as fast as untiled rendering, but can have significant memory savings, especially with large numbers of AOVs.

    NOTE:
        When stitching tiles, rendering to [MPlay|/mplay] will not be interactive.

Max Tile Resolution:
    When rendering a tiled image, this specifies the maximum resolution of each tile.  Limiting the resolution can make memory usage more consistent even if resolution changes.

Temporary Directory:
    Specify, where the intermediate tiles will be stored temporarily when rendering a tiled and stitched image.

Count:
    The number of tiles in X and Y resolution.  This number may be increased if the computed tile resolution is larger than __Max Tile Resolution__.

Index:
    This is the tile that `husk` should render.  The value should be between `0` and the total number of tiles (`Count.x*Count.y`).

Suffix:
    Each output image will be suffixed with this string.  The string supports the same variable expansion `husk` does on output images, but replacing the `%02d` with the tile index instead of the frame number.


=== Statistics ===

Print Command Line to Console:
    This option can be used to debug exactly what command the ROP is executing.

Verbose:
    #id: verbose
    How much information to print out while rendering. When you set __Verbose__ to `9`, you can see a list of pruned in primvars in the [Log Viewer|/ref/panes/logviewer] pane. Go to the pane's [Smallicon:BUTTONS/filter] search bar and enter `pruning` to filter the results and only show the primvars.

VEX Profiling:
    #id: vexprofile
    Profile VEX performance while rendering.  Normally, you should avoid "Profiling and NAN Detection" since it can impact performance (though it can be useful for debugging)

USD Trace:
    #id: husk_usdtracing

    This enables USD tracing.  This information can be used to profile USD performance in `husk`.

Chrome File:
    #id: husk_chromefile

    When using Chrome tracing, this is the file where the trace log should be stored.

Log Output:
    #id: husk_log

    Capture the output from `husk` and store the log in a file on disk.

Append to Log Instead of Overwriting:
    #id: husk_logappend

    Normally `husk` will overwrite the log file on each run.  This option will cause output to be appended to the text in existing files.

Output Log:
    #id: husk_stdout

    This is the file where normal messages should be saved.

Error Log:
    #id: husk_stderr

    This is the file to which error messages should be saved. If this is the same file specified for the Output Log, the output and error messages will be interleaved (in the same way they are written to the console).

=== Slap Comp ===

This tab specifies the [Slap Comp|/copernicus/slap_comp] operations to process after rendering. Each compositing operation is performed on the rendered image in sequence.

Disable All Slap Comp:
    #id: husk_disableslapcomp

    This will cause `husk` to disable *all* slap comp (including any `HoudiniImageFilterList` primitives defined on the stage).

==== Limitations ====

* The input names on the [Block Begin COP|Node:cop/block_begin] must match the names of AOVs produced by the renderer. For example, if there’s a depth input it looks for the depth AOV. The type of each input must also be consistent with its AOV.

* When using Slap Comp with `husk`, output AOVs must already exist and the output types in COPs must match the AOVs. Furthermore, the output resolution must be the same as the original resolution.

* Unlike in the Solaris viewport, the depth AOV isn’t exported by default by ROPs so you must turn it on. Add a [Karma Render Settings LOP|Node:lop/karmarendersettings] and go to __Image Output > AOVs > Utility__ to turn on __Depth (Camera Space)__.


Enabled:
    #id: husk_sc_enable
    Turn this Slap Comp operation on or off.

Source:
    #id: husk_sc_source
    You can choose, whether you want to use a source from a __File__ or a __COP Network__.

    File:
        Specify the COP network as an APEX graph from a disk file
    COP Network:
        Specify a path to a Block End LOP of a COP network.
    Filter List:
        Specify a path to an image filter list COP network.

File:
    #id: husk_sc_file
    The path to a geometry file on disk. The geometry file should contain an APEX graph of a COP network.

Cop Node:
    #id: husk_sc_cop
    The path to the Block End COP of a Compile Block COP.
    
Cop Node:
    #id: husk_sc_filterlist
    The path to the network node of an image filter list COP network.
    
Label:
    #id: husk_sc_label
    An optional label to identify this slap comp operation when `husk` prints out messages.

Map Input:
    #id: husk_sc_mapinput
    Sometimes, the AOV names being rendered don't match the input names for the Compile Block COP. This parameter lets you create a mapping of AOV names to COP input names. You can create a rule for each name you want to map.

Map Output:
    #id: husk_sc_mapoutput
    Sometimes, the names of an Output COP don't match the AOV names being rendered. This parameter lets you create a mapping of COP outputs to AOV names. You can create a rule for each name you want to map.

=== Extra Metadata ===

`husk` will add all the metadata defined on __Render Products__ and __Render Vars__.  However, in some cases, it's convenient to quickly add an extra metadata value.  This tab sets up the `--extra-metadata` command line option to `husk`.

Key:
    #id: husk_metadata_key

    Metadata uses key-value pairs and here you define the key.

    The metadata __Value__ will normally be stored as a string. However, it's possible to prefix the metadata which will cause `husk` to interpret the value as a different type. Types are:

    - `bool`
    - `int8`, `int16`, `int32`, `int64`, `vec2i`, `vec3i`, `vec4i`
    - `uint8`, `uint16`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `vec2u`, `vec3u`, `vec4u`
    - `half`, `real16`, `vec2h`, `vec3h`, `vec4h`
    - `float`, `real32`, `vec2f`, `vec3f`, `vec4f`, `mat3f`, `mat4f`
    - `double`, `real64`, `vec2d`, `vec3d`, `vec4d`, `mat3d`, `mat4d`
    - `string`
    - `clr3u8`, `clr4u8`, `clr3f`, `clr4f`, `clr3d`, `clr4d`
    - `point3f`, `point3d`
    - `normal3f`, `normal3d`
    - `vector3f`, `vector3d`

    For example: `int32 key` or `point3f key`

Value:
    #id: husk_metadata_value

    The value you want to store in the image metadata for the given __Key__. When you define a vector or color type, the value should be expressed as a JSON array like "`[0.4, 0.8, 1.3]`".

=== Karma ===

This tab contains a list of `husk` options that work specifically with the Karma delegate.

Percent of Samples:
    #id: karma_percentofsamples

    In order to remove noise, Karma will render a defined number of primary samples (camera rays).  Internally, the sampling patterns that Karma uses are tied closely to the number of primary samples.

    This option tells Karma to render a fraction of the primary samples.  When using a checkpoint file, this allows you to check the quality of the render, then resume the render if more samples are needed.

== Output ==

Render Command:
    #id: rendercommand
    This is the external command used to render. If this parameter is disabled (by turning off the __Run Command__ parameter) the command is not executed. The USD scene will still be output to disk, and the command will be output to the console (if __Print Command Line to Console__ is turned on), but the command will not actually be run. Disabling the running of the command also prevents the deletion of the generated USD files, even if they are in the Houdini temp directory. This mode can be very useful for debugging or for batch farm rendering.

Render Existing File:
    #id: dorenderexisting
    Use this option to render an existing USD file from disk rather than the input lop.

Save USD Before Rendering Existing File:
    #id: renderexistingandsaveusd
    When the __Render Existing File__ option is enabled, the saving of USD data from the __LOP path__ is normally disabled. Turn on this parameter to write the LOP data to disk before rendering the existing file. This is useful in cases where the LOP network is authoring data that is referenced by the __Render existing file__.

Resolver Context Asset Path:
    #id: resolvercontext

    This file path is passed to the render command line as the `resolver-context` option. This argument is used to create an asset resolver context that helps the asset resolver find files while composing the USD stage. The default of this parameter is an expression that returns the corresponding parameter on the LOP Network that contains the selected __LOP path__

Number of Resolver Context Strings:
    #id: resolvercontextstrings
    These arguments are passed to the render command line with the `render-context-string` option. The resolver context can be configured using multiple separate strings. Each string is used to configure one resolver. One string (with no URL prefix specified) is sent to the default resolver used for all asset paths that are not in URL format. Other strings can be paired with a URL prefix to configure the resolver associated with that prefix.

    If there is at least one non-empty resolver context string value provided, this takes precedence over any resolver context asset path, and the resolver context for the LOP stage will be created using the `ArResolver::CreateContextFromStrings` method instead of `ArResolver::CreateDefaultContextForAsset`.

    Enable:
        Individual resolver context configuration strings can be enabled or disabled with this toggle.

    URL Prefix:
        This string value will be sent to the resolver responsible for the specified URL prefix. If no prefix is provided, this string value will be sent to the default resolver.

    Value:
        The string value sent to the resolver determined by the URL Prefix.

Number of Variant Selection Fallback Rules:
    #id: variantselectioncount
    These parameters are passed to the render command line with the `variant-fallback` option. Configures what variant selection fallback values to use for specific variant sets when no explicit variant selection opinion is provided on a prim. These fallback rules are applied on top of any global variant selection fallbacks configured using the USD library plugin mechanism.

    Enable:
        A specific variant set fallback setting can be disabled with this toggle.

    Variant Set Name:
        Name of the variant set to configure.

    Fallback Selections:
        A space or comma separated list of variant selection values to attempt to use on this variant set when no explicit variant selection opinion is available.

Wait for Render to Complete:
    #id: soho_foreground

    Causes Houdini to freeze after starting the render process, and only resume when the renderer exits. (This is included mostly for parameter parity with the old Mantra render nodes. It may be useful to implement a crude form of dependency ordering when batch rendering.)

:include usd#alfprogress:

Create Intermediate Directories:
    #id: mkpath

    Create intermediate parent directories for output files as needed, such as for generated images.

Maximum Threads:
    Uses the `-j` command line option to `husk` to specify the maximum number of threads that process should use. This parameter can be enabled to ensure that some portion of the computer's processing power remains available for tasks other than the render. Positive values specify an absolute number of threads. Negative values indicate that the number of threads should be equal to the number of CPU cores on the machines minus the specified number.

:include usd#initsim:

:include usd#reportnetwork:

=== USD Export ===

:include usd#lopoutput:

Delete Files:
    #id: deletefiles

    Controls whether or not files (USD and VDB) saved to disk are deleted when the render process completes. In addition to deleting the files, any containing directories are also deleted if they are empty after deleting the USD. The modes of operation are:

    Delete if Saved to Temp Directory:
        Files saved to the Houdini temporary directory (`$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR`) are deleted. Files saved to any other directory are not deleted.

    Always Delete:
        All files generated by this ROP are deleted.

    Never Delete:
        Files generated by this ROP are not deleted.

:include usd#savestyle:

:include usd#usenetworksafesave:

:include usd#filtertimesamples:

:include usd#filtertimesamplespadding:

:include usd#extrafiles_group:

:include usd#outputprocessing_group:

USD Output Directory:
    The directory where any required USD files will be saved. If this directory is in the `$HOUDINI_TEMP_DIR`, it will be deleted automatically when the render is complete.

:include usd#layermetadata_group:

:include usd#contextoptions_group2:

== Scripts ==

Each script command refers to an `hscript` command which will be run, regardless of the expression language selected for the parameter. The resulting string will be run as an `hscript` command. It is possible to use the source __Hscript__ or __Python__ commands to perform complex processing.

The commands are always run when rendering occurs. The command checks the parameters of the output driver when it is rendering a range or sending output to a command.

Before the render occurs, Houdini will automatically set the current `hscript` directory to point to the output driver.

Pre-Render Script:
    This command is run before any USDs are generated. It is only run once per render.

Pre-Frame Script:
    This command is run before each USD is generated.

Post-Frame Script:
    This command is run after each USD is generated. Although the USD may have been generated, this does not necessarily mean that `husk` has finished rendering the image when this command is run.

Post-Render Script: 
    This command is run one time, after all USDs have been generated. Although the USD may have been generated, this does not necessarily mean that `husk` has finished rendering the image when this command is run.
